name: Axams
kurzbeschreibung: Popular holiday destination at the foot of the Axamer Lizum, host of the 1964 and 1976 Winter Olympics.
beschreibung:
Overview

Axams is a historic municipality in the Innsbruck-Land district, situated at an altitude of approximately 874 meters on a sunny plateau of the Western Low Mountain Terrace. With over 6,300 residents, the town lies just ten kilometers southwest of the Tyrolean provincial capital Innsbruck. To the south, the municipality is dominated by the dramatic limestone ridges of the Kalkkögel, famously referred to as the North Tyrolean Dolomites. Tucked behind these peaks lies the high-alpine bowl of Axamer Lizum, ranging from 1,560 to 2,340 meters in elevation. Axams seamlessly unites rich village traditions and UNESCO cultural heritage with prestigious Olympic winter sports history, offering prime year-round recreation on Innsbruck's doorstep. The municipality belongs to the Innsbruck region.

History

The fertile plateau of Axams has been continuously inhabited since the Bronze and Hallstatt ages, as confirmed by archaeological excavations. The settlement was first documented between 935 and 955 as Ouxuuenes in episcopal charters from Brixen. As early as the 8th century, Axams served as a Carolingian mother parish for the surrounding plateaus, while the Bavarian convent of Frauenchiemsee held judicial authority until 1806. Emperor Maximilian I favored the Axamer Lizum basin as a preferred royal chamois hunting ground in the late 15th century. The town earned global prominence during the 1964 and 1976 Innsbruck Olympic Winter Games, when Axamer Lizum served as the primary venue for women's alpine ski races and men's technical events, where icons such as Christl Haas and Rosi Mittermaier claimed Olympic gold. The Baroque parish church of Saint John the Baptist with its 74-meter Gothic steeple crowns the village center, while the ancient carnival ritual of Wampelerreiten was recognized as UNESCO Intangible Cultural Heritage in 2016.

How to Get There

By car, Axams is reached from the west via the Inntal motorway A12, exiting at Zirl-Ost/Kematen and following the L12 road for ten minutes. From Innsbruck or the Brenner motorway, exit at Innsbruck-West/Völs and follow the L56 road across the plateau in about fifteen minutes. A well-maintained eight-kilometer mountain road connects the village center directly to Axamer Lizum. Public transport travelers take frequent VVT regional bus line 4162 from Innsbruck Hauptbahnhof, which departs every 15 to 30 minutes, supplemented by free winter ski shuttles to the ski lifts.

Tips

The crown jewel is the Axamer Lizum ski area, offering forty kilometers of pistes and the state-of-the-art ten-passenger Hoadlbahn gondola, whisking visitors up to the Hoadl plateau at 2,340 meters in under six minutes. The Hoadl-Haus mountain restaurant features a panoramic terrace overlooking the dramatic Kalkkögel needles and the Inn Valley. Summer draws hikers to the Kalkkögel panorama path, challenging via ferratas, and scenic trails to the Kemater Alm. The Axams Leisure Center invites guests to relax with an indoor pool, heated outdoor pool, sauna complex, and sunbathing lawn, while the local heritage and nativity museum showcases fine folk art.
